content.text: Travel2's ~200ms outbound GETs to route-service show a server span that starts ~210ms after the client span, and the server itself only takes ~2ms. That delay is on the caller side. I'll compare this against normal traces.

input.reflection: Findings so far: (1) route-plan getCheapestRoutes/getQuickestRoutes: ~1.75s idle gap between its first downstream call (station idlist, ~20ms) and second downstream call (basic/travels). Downstream spans are fast, so the wait is in route-plan itself (before issuing the 2nd call). Same in every sampled trace. (2) travel2 adminQueryAll: sequential GET calls to ts-route-service; each client span ~200-420ms but the server span (route-service, pod mhvh7) takes only ~2-7ms and starts ~210ms AFTER client start. So ~200ms of delay occurs before the request reaches route-service, on the travel2 side (client/pool/network). Need normal baseline for travel2->route-service client-vs-server gap and route-plan gaps to confirm these are abnormal, and check whether route-service's pod or the route-plan/travel2 pods show something specific (e.g., a single pod on a different node). Also the many errors 'Route not found' in route-service may be baseline.

content.text:
The degradation is pure latency, with no 5xx or error status codes, and comes from two independent faults. Both sit inside a service's own code or outbound call, not in the services that show the symptoms.

## Affected endpoints (user-facing)

| Endpoint (ui-dashboard entry) | Normal | Abnormal | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST /api/v1/travelplanservice/travelPlan/cheapest | ~75 ms avg, p95 ~190 ms | ~1.5–1.8 s | Degraded |
| POST /api/v1/travelplanservice/travelPlan/quickest | ~70 ms avg, p95 ~130 ms | ~1.8 s | Degraded |
| GET /api/v1/admintravelservice/admintravel | ~63 ms avg | ~0.7 s avg, p95 ~1.5 s | Degraded |
| POST /travelPlan/minStation, /users/login, /preserve, /adminuserservice/users | normal | normal | Not affected |

## Fault 1: ts-route-plan-service stalls inside its cheapest/quickest route handlers (origin)

- `RoutePlanController.getCheapestRoutes` and `getQuickestRoutes` take ~1.3–1.8 s of own time, but their child spans total only ~40 ms. Normal is ~60 ms with ~57 ms of children.
- In a sampled trace, the first downstream call (station idlist) finishes around 14.534 s. The second call (basic/travels) doesn't start until 16.285 s. That ~1.75 s gap is inside route-plan's own code, before it issues the call. The downstream spans are fast (~20 ms).
- The same ~1.75 s idle gap shows up in every sampled slow trace. `getMinStopStations` is unaffected.
- ts-travel-plan-service is a propagation hop: its POST to route-plan takes ~1.8 s, and route-plan's server span starts with ~0 ms delay, so travel-plan is waiting on route-plan.
- The route-plan pod shows no restarts and low CPU.

## Fault 2: ts-travel2-service outbound calls to ts-route-service are delayed before they are sent (origin)

- Normal: travel2 → route-service client and server spans start within ~0.1 ms of each other.
- Abnormal: about a third of travel2's GET calls to route-service have a ~200–420 ms gap before the server span starts. The server itself responds in ~2–7 ms.
- Another ~10 of 30 sampled GET calls have no server span at all.
- Other callers of route-service (ui-dashboard, basic, travel, route-plan, admin-route) show no such delay, so route-service itself is not the problem.
- Travel2's calls to basic, train, and station are normal.
- Travel2's `adminQueryAll` averages ~450 ms (max ~650 ms). That drives ts-admin-travel-service's `getAllTravels` (~790 ms), which drives the admintravel endpoint.

## Ruled out

- **Shared node:** the affected pods are on different nodes (route-plan .65, travel2 .38, travel-plan .41, admin-travel .60, route-service .88).
- **Pod saturation or restarts:** CPU limit utilization is low and the restart counts match normal.
- **Route-not-found errors:** these appear in route-service and travel2 logs, but at a lower rate than in the normal baseline, so they are noise.

## Caveats

- The telemetry shows where the time goes but not why. Neither the route-plan gap nor the travel2 pre-send delay has an explaining log message or metric.
- Fault 2 is located on travel2's side of the travel2→route-service edge, based on the caller-side timing. It is not confirmed as travel2's own code rather than the network path between the two pods.
- Both faults could be validated further with pod-level profiling or thread dumps of route-plan and travel2 during the slow window.
